title: Offline-first foundations: asset acquisition, research providers, creator review

lanes.title: Asset acquisition pipeline and rights-evidence handling (offline, transport-injected)
acceptance_criteria: A new module orchestrator/assets/acquisition.py provides an explicit acquire step: it runs the existing triage/rights decision first, fetches only PERMITTED candidates, records QUARANTINE candidates as quarantined records with their reason codes and never fetches them, and never fetches REJECT candidates; unknown rights are never permission

Fetching goes through an injected Transport protocol (no real network code is exercised anywhere): https-only URLs, a per-provider host allow-list, a maximum byte size, a content-type allow-list per media type, a timeout parameter; the file is written atomically (temporary file, sha256 verified, then moved into the library layout), refuses path traversal, never overwrites an existing asset, and detects duplicates by sha256

Every failure path (transport error, truncated or oversize download, wrong content type, hash mismatch, library write error) leaves no partial file behind and records a scrubbed error that contains no credential-like text; each path has its own test

Rights-evidence handling: the licence evidence captured at acquisition (source URL, retrieval date, a hash of the licence text snapshot, the verifier) is stored with the asset; a re-verification function detects licence drift (stored hash differs from the current text) and moves the asset to quarantine without deleting it; human attestations keep working through the existing Attestation model

A concrete offline LocalFolderProvider searches a directory of user-supplied files described by sidecar rights files (documented, validated schema, strict: unknown keys and missing rights are quarantined, never permitted); acquisition copies, and original files are never modified, moved or deleted (a test hashes the originals before and after)

At least one open-licence catalogue adapter (Openverse or Wikimedia Commons) is implemented as a pure request builder plus response parser over the injected transport and tested only against fixture payloads authored from the public API documentation; the documentation and the report state NOT TESTED against the live service

A single function find_and_acquire(request, registry, library, transport, context) runs search, triage and acquisition and returns a deterministic report listing acquired, quarantined, rejected and failed items with reasons; ordering is stable across runs

At least 60 new offline tests in orchestrator/tests/test_asset_acquisition.py; one test proves no network is touched (socket creation is patched to fail); synthetic tiny files only, no real media; the existing test_assets.py passes (it may be extended, never weakened)

ASSETS.md documents the acquisition flow, the sidecar schema, the failure behaviour and what is IMPLEMENTED versus NOT TESTED (live providers, real media); open questions are listed, not decided; the lane report lists anything needing a decision from Lukas

lanes.title: Concrete research providers, caching, budgets and the pipeline stage adapter (offline, transport-injected)
acceptance_criteria: At least four concrete providers are implemented as pure request builders plus response parsers over an injected Transport protocol: Crossref and OpenAlex (scholarly metadata), the MediaWiki API (encyclopedic) and the Wikimedia pageviews API (trend signal); every parser converts into the existing RawHit and goes through the existing coercion and validation (coerce_hit); malformed, oversize or hostile payloads are quarantined with a reason, never raised to the caller

Provider fixtures are authored from the public API documentation and clearly labelled as such; the documentation and the report state NOT TESTED against the live services; no API key, credential or real network call exists anywhere in code or tests

The existing source-quality machinery in sources.py is applied to every provider hit (tier and quality assigned, low-quality or unverifiable sources quarantined or flagged exactly as the existing rules specify) with a test matrix covering every provider and every tier outcome

Budgets and resilience: ResearchBudget limits are enforced per provider and per run; a deterministic retry/backoff policy uses an injectable clock and sleeper (tests never sleep); a per-provider circuit breaker stops calling a failing provider and records why; every error message is scrubbed

A caching layer stores provider responses on disk keyed by provider, normalized query and date with a TTL, writes atomically, never caches an error, and a ReplayTransport serves recorded responses so a research run is reproducible offline; tests cover hits, misses, expiry, corrupted cache files and concurrent writers

A pipeline stage function run_research_stage(brief, providers, budget, today) returns the existing research->creative_director contract packet; the packet produced for every existing fixture is byte-for-byte unchanged, the contract version is not changed, and a test validates the packet shape (including the safety fields) against the documented contract without importing creative_director

At least 70 new offline tests in orchestrator/tests/test_research_providers.py; one test proves no network is touched (socket creation is patched to fail); all existing tests in test_research.py still pass (they may be extended, never weakened)

RESEARCH.md documents the providers, limits, cache and stage adapter, with IMPLEMENTED versus NOT TESTED labels; open questions are listed, not decided; the lane report lists anything needing a decision from Lukas

lanes.title: Creator review workflow for Creator DNA: queue, decisions, offline review sheet and CLI
acceptance_criteria: A new module orchestrator/creator_dna/review.py builds a deterministic review queue from a DNAStore: traits awaiting confirmation, evidence flagged unattributed or legacy_possible_revocation, and traits with conflicting counter-evidence; every item has a stable id, the trait statement, the evidence quotes and timecodes (references only, no media access) and the reason it was queued; the same store always yields the same queue in the same order

A decision API applies creator decisions (confirm a trait, reject evidence, restore evidence, correct a trait statement, defer) exclusively through the existing event-log methods and rules (schema v4: restore never undoes an attribution revocation); every decision needs an explicit actor and a note, is idempotent where the event model allows it, and is replay-safe (a store rebuilt from its log equals the live store)

An offline review sheet export (Markdown plus JSON) lets the creator read the queue away from the computer, and a decisions-file import validates the whole file first and then applies it all-or-nothing: one bad entry applies nothing and every error is reported with its line; a dry-run mode reports what would change and writes nothing

A CLI python -m creator_dna review (queue, export, apply, status) with --store, --dry-run and an explicit --yes before any write, deterministic output, and non-zero exit codes on invalid input, mirroring the style of the creator_state CLI; no command ever deletes evidence or events

The creator's identity (open question Q39) and the review workflow shape (Q30) are NOT decided: actor is a required explicit string that the module neither infers nor validates against any identity source; the open questions are recorded in the documentation and in the report as decisions for Lukas

Existing event semantics and schema version 4 are unchanged unless a change is unavoidable and justified in the report; all existing tests in test_creator_dna.py, test_speaker_attribution.py and test_integration_phase2_phase3.py pass unmodified; speaker_attribution, media_analysis and every other package are not edited

At least 50 new offline tests in orchestrator/tests/test_creator_dna_review.py including determinism of the queue, replay equality after a batch of decisions, an interrupted or partially invalid decisions file leaving the log byte-identical, and the all-or-nothing import; synthetic data only, no real recordings or transcripts

CREATOR_DNA.md documents the review workflow, the sheet and decision-file formats and the CLI, with IMPLEMENTED versus NOT TESTED labels (nothing is VERIFIED on real data) and the extension point for transcript review once a transcription engine exists; the lane report lists anything needing a decision from Lukas
